we have developed a computational scheme that can be used to analyze the electromagnetic properties of a deformed cavity by using the previously developed multiphysics finite element models, but with a mesh improvement to avoid the unphysical results on greatly deformed structures.

the multi-physics computational scheme for superconducting radiofrequency cavities can be used to compute the electromagnetic characteristic of the deformed cavities, and the interior solid elements, assigned with a negligible rigidities, are adjusted to a reasonable shape as the external loadings are applied on the cavity structure.
the multiphysics computation with finite element models has been successfully applied to design the superconducting radiofrequency cavity.

the design of a superconducting radiofrequency cavity for a synchrotron radiation facility, the China Spallation Neutron Source.
the development of a multiphysics computational scheme for superconducting radiofrequency cavities.

the application of a finite-element method for multi-physics computation on the design of a superconducting radiofrequency cavity, with the aim of obtaining more accurate results for the cavity deformation and electromagnetic characteristics.

the proposed computational scheme for multi-physic coupling is capable of computing the electromagnetic characteristics of a superconducting radiofrequency cavity with a reasonable accuracy.
the proposed method can provide a more accurate result than the previous method, and it is more efficient and reliable than the traditional finite-element method.
this new method is an effective and reliable tool to compute the multiphysics characteristics of deformed superconducting radiofrequency cavities.

the multi-physics computation with finite elements is a powerful tool for cavity design and the meshing of solid elements in the cavity vacuum is necessary for a greatly deformed cavity.
the computational method for the multiphysic simulation of a superconducting radio frequency cavity can be improved by meshing the vacuum with solid elements.

the multiphysics computation with the finite-element method is a powerful and flexible tool for the design of the superconducting radiofrequency cavities, and the proposed method could be applied to other similar problems in which the structural deformation is significant and needs to be taken into consideration.
